---
title: "Shiny module trees"
guide-section: "Shiny"
jupyter: python3
---

`call_tree_dir()` and `call_tree_app()` draw the call tree of a Shiny for Python app. The first reads `.py` files on disk. The second inspects a `shiny.App` object.

## A small app

```{python}
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

app_dir = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) / "counter"
app_dir.mkdir()
(app_dir / "__init__.py").write_text("")
(app_dir / "modules.py").write_text('''
from shiny import module, render, ui


def log_msg(msg):
    return msg


@module.ui
def counter_ui(label="Count"):
    log_msg("counter_ui")
    return ui.input_action_button("go", label)


@module.server
def counter_server(input, output, session):
    log_msg("counter_server")

    @render.text
    def count():
        return str(input.go())
''')
_ = (app_dir / "app.py").write_text('''
from shiny import App, ui

from .modules import counter_server, counter_ui, log_msg


def app_ui():
    return ui.page_fluid(counter_ui("a"))


def app_server(input, output, session):
    log_msg("server")
    counter_server("a")


app = App(app_ui(), app_server)
''')
```

## From files

`call_tree_dir()` parses every `.py` file under `path` without importing it. It links each top level function to the other top level functions its body calls or names:

```{python}
from callgrove import call_tree_dir

call_tree_dir(app_dir, root="app_server")
```

`log_msg` shows up under every node. `exclude` drops it and moves its children up:

```{python}
call_tree_dir(app_dir, root="app_server", exclude="log_msg")
```

When two files define a function with the same name, `call_tree_dir()` warns and keeps the one parsed last.

## Modules only

`modules_only=True` keeps the root and the functions decorated with `@module.ui` or `@module.server`. Every other function is spliced out and its children move up:

```{python}
call_tree_dir(app_dir, root="app_ui", modules_only=True)
```

## From an App object

`call_tree_app()` takes the server out of a `shiny.App` and follows the names it references. Only functions defined in the app's own package join the tree, so `shiny.ui` calls are left out. The app is never run:

```{python}
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, str(app_dir.parent))
from counter.app import app
from callgrove import call_tree_app

call_tree_app(app, exclude="log_msg")
```

`App()` renders a static UI when it is created, so the function behind it is gone. The tree above has no UI branch, and `call_tree_app()` warns about it. Pass the function's name with `ui_fun` to add the UI branch:

```{python}
call_tree_app(app, ui_fun="app_ui", exclude="log_msg")
```

Module functions are found even though Shiny wraps them, because `call_tree_app()` peels the decorator off before reading the source.

## Recap

`call_tree_dir()` works on source you haven't installed. `call_tree_app()` works on an app you can import. Both return a `CallTree` and take `modules_only`, `exclude`, and `max_depth`.
